claim: This finding from the previous review no longer holds at the reviewed head: 1. The docstring in `src/sqllens/agent/integrations/postgres/sql_runner.py` promises more than the connection-string path delivers. Line 57 still says `**kwargs: Additional psycopg2 connection parameters (sslmode, connect_timeout, etc.)`, but when the runner is built from a DSN only `connect_timeout` is copied into `_connection_options` and forwarded to `psycopg2.connect`. prior_evidence: 2. A malformed DSN now fails when the runner is constructed instead of when a query runs. Line 73 calls `psycopg2.extensions.parse_dsn(connection_string)` with no guard, so a DSN psycopg2 cannot parse raises `psycopg2.ProgrammingError` out of `PostgresRunner.__init__`, and therefore out of `build_sql_runner`. The final-pass reviewer checked the boundary and found it covered: `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:227-231` catches failures during agent construction and returns a sanitized internal-error message without echoing the DSN. The remaining cost is that the user sees a generic internal error rather than "your database URL is malformed", that the `Raises:` docstring still points at `run_sql`, and that the logged exception text can quote offending DSN tokens. No test exercises a DSN that `parse_dsn` rejects. (raised by 3/5 agents)

claim: An empty PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT is treated by this code as unset so the five-second default is injected, and that treatment matches how libpq handles an empty PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT value.
verify_against: libpq PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT handling versus the falsy environment check in PostgresRunner.__init__
verify_hint: Check both `os.environ.get("PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT")` guards in `PostgresRunner.__init__` against libpq's documented connect_timeout parsing
prior_evidence: sql_runner.py:78 and :90 use `not os.environ.get("PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT")`. Empty string is falsy so the 5s default is applied. But whitespace-only (e.g. " ") is truthy, so it is NOT treated as unset and no default is applied; the claim's whitespace part is wrong. On libpq: getenv returns non-NULL for an empty value so libpq takes it as the set value, and as I recall an empty connect_timeout parses to 0 (no timeout). That would differ from the 5s default applied here, so the 'must match libpq' part is doubtful too. I did not run libpq or read its source in this environment, so that part rests on recall.

claim: PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT is read only at PostgresRunner construction time to decide default injection, and the documented behaviour matches what later environment changes do to subsequent run_sql connections.
source_excerpt: if "connect_timeout" not in kwargs and not os.environ.get("PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT"):
verify_against: PostgresRunner.__init__ environment reads versus libpq's per-connect reading of PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT, and the configuration docs
verify_hint: Check the individual-parameter branch guard in `PostgresRunner.__init__` and the PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT description in `docs/external/configuration.md`
prior_evidence: sql_runner.py:78,90 check os.environ PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT only at construction, to decide whether to inject a default connect_timeout. But when the env var is set at construction, no connect_timeout is stored (lines 78, 90), and run_sql (lines 122/124) calls psycopg2.connect, where libpq reads PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT at each connect. So later env changes do affect later connections (e.g. unset later gives no timeout; changed value takes effect). Conversely, if unset at construction, the injected default of _DEFAULT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS overrides a later-set env var. The claim is only true for the injection decision, not for connection behaviour.

claim: This finding from the previous review no longer holds at the reviewed head: 1. `PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT` is read once, when the runner is constructed, at lines 78 and 90 of `src/sqllens/agent/integrations/postgres/sql_runner.py`, and only checked for presence. If the variable is unset at construction, the hard-coded five-second default is injected and wins over any value exported later. An unparseable value such as `abc` suppresses the default and is handed to libpq unremarked. `docs/external/configuration.md:49` presents the variable as a plain override with no note about when it is read. One checklist verifier disagreed in part: because libpq itself re-reads the variable at each connect, a value changed after construction can still take effect on the connect call when no timeout was injected, so the lifecycle claim holds only for the decision to inject the default. (raised by 1/5 agents)
